subject: Clarify: training exclusion, snapshots, and deletion timelines
messages:
From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@medalpha.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: MedAlpha Legal <privacy@medalpha.com>
Date: Fri, 8 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on retention vs training — snapshots and backups

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the product walkthrough yesterday. Legal had one follow-up that I couldn’t resolve on the call: your team’s public statement that Redwood "does not train on customer-provided data" — can you clarify how that applies to the operational artifacts we discussed (snapshots, periodic backups, debug archives, and ephemeral KV snapshots)? Specifically: 

- If we ask for deletion of a dataset, what happens to a snapshot that was taken for debugging two weeks earlier?
- Do backups or crash dumps ever flow into model training pipelines (even in an anonymized/aggregate form)?
- Is there any retention window where data might be used for internal tooling that could indirectly feed model improvement?

We’re collecting this for MedAlpha’s privacy impact assessment. Attaching our high-level checklist — appreciate any detail you can provide.

— Oliver

(Attachment: medalpha-privacy-checklist.pdf)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@medalpha.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 May 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on retention vs training — snapshots and backups

Oliver — thanks, great questions. I wanted to give a concise operational answer and then follow up with a short note on edge cases. High level: Redwood does not use customer request/response data to train or improve our public models. That guarantee extends to derived training pipelines we run internally. The practical implications: 

- Snapshots & debug archives: these are retained for a short operational window strictly for debugging and incident response. They are tagged as "customer-owned" and reside in a segregated store. When you request deletion we first tombstone the references and then schedule secure deletion from all operational stores.

- Backups & crash dumps: periodic backups are encrypted and treated as part of our disaster-recovery footprint. We do not route backup material into any model training or research pipelines. Crash dumps that might contain payloads are scrubbed/scoped and only used by the SRE/infra team for root-cause analysis.

- Indirect tooling / telemetry: aggregated telemetry (e.g., latency histograms, token-level performance metrics that have been aggregated across tenants) can be used to tune the serving runtime; this is strictly aggregated and never includes customer text payloads. No de-identified or pseudonymized copies of customer text are introduced into model training.

I’ll loop in Neha and Ben for the procedural details (retention windows, tombstone schedules, and ATO for snapshots).

Best,
Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Oliver Park <oliver.park@medalpha.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 May 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on retention vs training — snapshots and backups

Hi all — adding the operational timeline and list of safeguards so Legal can map to your checklist: 

1) Snapshot lifecycle: 
- Short-term debug snapshots: 14 days by default. These are single-tenant snapshots kept to reproduce incidents and support bugfixes. They are stored in an isolated bucket with strict ACLs.
- Extended snapshots: only created with customer consent (e.g., for extended troubleshooting) and will have an explicit TTL agreed in writing.

2) Tombstone & deletion flow: 
- When a deletion or "no-train" request is received we immediately mark all references as tombstoned (0–24h).
- A background job expunges tombstoned artifacts from live stores within 48–72h.
- Copies in disaster-recovery backups are flagged and removed at the next backup rotation; we can accelerate this on request for managed Dedicated/Private customers.

3) Snapshots/backups and training: 
- Explicit policy: Under no circumstances do we feed snapshots, backups, or crash dumps into training pipelines. Internal research uses curated public datasets or synthetic data; any internal models are trained on datasets that are explicitly approved and documented.

4) Auditability & proof: 
- We maintain an audit trail for delete/tombstone actions (who, when, artifact id).
- For customers needing attestation, we can provide a deletion certificate and a CSV of artifact ids removed.

Attachments: I’ve attached the current snapshot retention diagram and the deletion playbook (redwood-snapshot-policy.pdf).

Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
